text: 🇲🇽🌎 "Sovereignty springs from the people. Only the people of Mexico can define their present and their destiny — no elite." — Claudia Sheinbaum, "Honestidad y Resultados," Mérida, Yucatán Two years into her government, Sheinbaum toured the states to give a public account of results. In Yucatán she grounded sovereignty in the words of Hidalgo from the early 1800s.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Tariffs and all, Mexico is still the US's #1 trade partner</u>

Trump's tariff war hasn't dislodged it: Mexico ran $493.7 billion in bilateral trade with the US in the first half of 2026 — ahead of Canada ($376B) and nearly triple China ($184.8B) — with record exports of $298.2 billion. El Financiero's honest caveat: strip out low-value computer and server assembly and export growth is closer to 5% — the value-added climb Mexico's nearshoring push still has to win.

🇲🇽🏙️ <u>Mexico City invests in prevention, not just response</u>

Ahead of the Sept 19 national drill — the anniversary of both the 1985 and 2017 earthquakes — Clara Brugada's government is putting 700 million pesos into Mexico City housing units this year: 2,500 emergency backpacks and gas detectors handed out, 1,222 buildings already upgraded in Cuauhtémoc, free firefighter safety inspections. "Prevention is a fundamental tool for reducing risk," said civil-protection chief Myriam Urzúa.

🇲🇽🇺🇸 <u>179 years on: remember who invaded whom</u>

On Sept 13, 1847, six teenage cadets — the youngest just 12 — died defending Chapultepec Castle against the invading US Army. Months later the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo stripped away more than half of Mexico's territory, shrinking it from 4.5 to 1.9 million km². The same power now musing about "sending troops" over cartels once took half the country by force.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>Rebuilding the grid the country owns</u>

Mexico is reversing Peña Nieto's energy sell-off: the 2025-2039 plan puts 72.47 billion pesos into 49,288 public works — 97 new substations, 42,221 electrification projects — by 2030. The historic electricians' union SME is signing on. "We're ready to join this great labor crusade to strengthen the electrical sector," said its leader Martín Esparza, invoking the 1960 nationalization. Public power, built with Mexican workers and Mexican materials.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Volkswagen workers say no: 67% reject the raise</u>

At VW Puebla, 4,327 of 5,925 unionized workers — 67% — voted down the company's "10.04%" offer, because the real wage bump was just 4.30%, the rest dressed up as savings-fund tweaks and a one-time bonus. Sitiavw keeps its strike notice alive for Sept 17 and is demanding a straight 6% and contract reviews every 12 months, not every 18.

🇲🇽🌬️ <u>Mexico bets big on wind — 84% more capacity by 2030</u>

While Washington retreats from clean energy, Mexico is scaling it up under state planning. Sener's Jorge Islas says wind capacity will jump 84% by 2030, adding 6,860 MW — 4,701 MW already assigned to 17 new wind farms — pushing renewables from 24.61% of generation today to over 38%. Planned by the state, not left to the market.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexican Industry Posts Its Fastest Growth in 33 Months</u>

Mexico's industrial output rose 2.4% year-on-year in July — its strongest annual growth in 33 months, per INEGI data reported by El Economista — led by construction up 6.7% and mining up 1.6%. Month-on-month, industry gained 0.5%, with construction (+0.9%) and manufacturing (+0.7%) driving the advance, as the peso holds near 16.9 to the dollar, its best level of the year.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Fuel-Theft Crackdown: 7.9 Million Liters Seized in Guanajuato</u>

The FGR raided a property in Salamanca, Guanajuato and found a five-meter vertical tank holding 35,000 liters of stolen diesel — pushing the total seized in the state to nearly 7.9 million liters, worth over 189 million pesos, across 106 raids this administration. Investigators also hauled off a computer and DVR to trace the distribution network.

🇲🇽📚 <u>OECD Says Mexico's Public-School Model Is Closing the Equity Gap</u>

Mexico's Nueva Escuela Mexicana is drawing international recognition: in PISA, the science gap between advantaged and disadvantaged students is 68 points, well below the 85-point OECD average; 82% of Mexican students say they ask teachers for help (OECD 77%), and only 11% see school as a waste of time versus 24% across the OECD. Sheinbaum called it "a distinct pedagogy, recognized internationally" — not the old teacher-centered classroom.
